Surah Yunus [Meccan, except verses 40, 94, 95 and 96, which are Medinan; it has 109 or 110 verses; it was revealed after the Night Journey (al-Isra')]

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this. ﴿These﴾, i.e., these ﴿verses of the Book﴾, the Qur'an. The genitive construction here is in the sense of "from" (i.e., verses from the Book), and ﴿the Wise﴾ means the perfectly arranged (al-muhkam).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 2:

﴿Was it a wonder for the people﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, an interrogative of denial. The prepositional phrase ﴿for the people﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to his saying ﴿a wonder﴾. With the accusative (naṣb) reading, it is the predicate (khabar) of kāna (was); with the nominative (rafʿ) reading, it is its subject (ism), and the predicate is then its subject, on the first reading. ﴿That We revealed﴾, i.e., Our revelation, ﴿to a man from among them﴾, Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿That﴾ is explanatory (mufassira). ﴿Warn﴾, i.e., frighten, ﴿the people﴾, the disbelievers, with the punishment, ﴿and give good news to those who believe that﴾, i.e., that ﴿they have a sure standing (qadam ṣidq, salaf ṣidq) with their Lord﴾, i.e., a good reward for the deeds they have sent forward. ﴿The disbelievers said: Indeed, this﴾, the Qur'an containing that, ﴿is clearly a magician﴾, manifest. In another reading it is "a magician" (sāḥir), and the one referred to is the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ of the days of this world, i.e., in their measure, for there were then no sun or moon. Had He willed, He could have created them in an instant; but His choosing otherwise is to teach His creation deliberateness (al-tathabbut). ﴿Then He istawa (rose/settled) over the Throne﴾ in a manner befitting Him. ﴿He arranges the affair﴾ among the creatures. ﴿There is no﴾ [the word] ﴿intercessor﴾ (shafi') ﴿except after His permission﴾ — a refutation of their claim that the idols intercede for them. ﴿That is﴾ the Creator who arranges [all things], ﴿Allah, your Lord; so worship Him﴾ — make Him one (wahhidu-hu). ﴿Will you not remember?﴾ — with the assimilation of the taʾ (ta') of the original (tatadhakkarun) into the dhal (dhal).

﴿إليه﴾ [Exalted is He], ﴿مرجعكم جميعا﴾ [your return, all of you], ﴿وعد الله حقا﴾ [the promise of Allah is true]: these are two verbal nouns (مصدران, maṣdarān) in the accusative, governed by their implied verbs (بفعلهما المقدر, bi-fi'lihimā al-muqaddar). ﴿إنه﴾ [Indeed He], with a kasra on the إ as a resumption (استئنافا, isti'nāfan), a new sentence; and with a fatḥa on the إ on the basis of an implied لام (lām). ﴿يبدأ الخلق﴾ [originates creation], meaning He originated it by bringing it into being. ﴿ثم يعيده﴾ [then repeats it] by resurrection. ﴿ليجزي﴾ [so that He may recompense], meaning reward: ﴿الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط﴾ [those who believe and do righteous deeds, with justice], ﴿والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم﴾ [and those who disbelieve, for them is a drink of boiling water], meaning water that has reached the utmost degree of heat, ﴿وعذاب أليم﴾ [and a painful punishment], meaning causing pain, ﴿بما كانوا يكفرون﴾ [because they used to disbelieve], meaning because of their disbelief.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 10, verse 5:

﴿He it is Who made the sun a shining radiance﴾ (ḍiyāʾ, dhāt ḍiyāʾ, i.e., possessing light), ﴿and the moon a light﴾ (nūran), ﴿and determined for it stations﴾ (qaddarahu, i.e., from the standpoint that He made it travel), ﴿stations﴾ (manāzil), twenty-eight stations, in twenty-eight nights of each month, and it hides for two nights if the month is thirty days, or for one night if the month is twenty-nine days. ﴿That you might know﴾ (li-taʿlamū), by this, ﴿the number of years and the reckoning.﴾ ﴿God did not create that﴾ (mentioned above) ﴿except in truth﴾ (illā bil-ḥaqq), not in vain, exalted is He above that. ﴿He details﴾ (yufaṣṣil), with the ya' and the nun (both readings), He makes clear ﴿the signs for a people who know﴾ (yaʿlamūn), who reflect (yatadabbarūn).

Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, by going and coming, and by increase and decrease. ﴿And what Allah has created in the heavens﴾ of angels, sun, moon, stars and other things, ﴿and﴾ in ﴿the earth﴾ of animals, mountains, seas, rivers, trees and other things, ﴿are surely signs﴾ indications of His power, exalted is He, ﴿for a people who fear﴾ for a people who fear Him and so believe. He singled them out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ [i.e., do not expect the Resurrection (al-ba'th)] ﴿and are content with the worldly life﴾ [in place of the Hereafter (al-akhirah), because they deny it] ﴿and are at rest in it﴾ [they settle down in it] ﴿and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ [the proofs of Our oneness (wahdaniyyah)] ﴿heedless﴾ [neglecting to reflect upon them]

Translation:

﴿Those, their abode is the Fire, because of what they used to earn﴾ from polytheism and sins.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 9:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord guides them﴾ means: guides them (yurshiduhum) ﴿their Lord﴾ (Rabbuhum) ﴿by their faith﴾ (bi-imanihim) in Him (bihi), by making for them a light by which they are guided on the Day of Resurrection.

Their call therein: their request in Paradise, for whatever they desire, will be that they say, ﴿Glory be to You, O Allah﴾, meaning, O Allah. So whenever they request something, they find it before them. ﴿And their greeting therein will be﴾ among themselves: ﴿Peace﴾. ﴿And the last of their call will be that﴾ (an explanatory "that," mufassira), ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. It was revealed when the polytheists were hastening the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 11:

﴿And if Allah were to hasten for mankind the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, i.e., as they seek to hasten it. ﴿He would have decreed for them their term﴾ — the verb is read in the passive and in the active voice — ﴿their term﴾ — with the noun in the nominative and in the accusative — by destroying them, but He gives them respite instead. ﴿So We leave﴾, i.e., We abandon ﴿those who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, i.e., vacillating and bewildered.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 12:

﴿And when harm touches man﴾ the disbeliever, ﴿harm﴾ meaning sickness and poverty, ﴿he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ i.e., lying down, ﴿or sitting or standing﴾ i.e., in every state. ﴿Then when We remove from him his harm, he passes on﴾ in his disbelief, ﴿as if﴾ (kaʾann, here the light form, whose noun is omitted, i.e., "as if he") ﴿he had never called upon Us concerning a harm that touched him. Thus﴾ as He made appealing to him the supplication at the time of harm and the turning away at the time of ease, ﴿is made attractive to the extravagant﴾ the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 13:

﴿And We certainly destroyed the generations﴾ the nations ﴿before you﴾ O people of Makkah ﴿when they did wrong﴾ by associating partners (with Allah) ﴿and﴾ their messengers had come to them ﴿with clear proofs﴾ that indicate their truthfulness ﴿and they would not have believed﴾ a coordination with "they did wrong" ﴿Thus﴾ as We destroyed those ﴿We recompense the criminal people﴾ the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 14:

﴿Then We made you﴾ O people of Makkah ﴿successors﴾ plural of khalifah ﴿in the earth after them,﴾ ﴿so that We may see how you act﴾ in it, and whether you will take heed from them and thus believe in Our messengers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 15:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, clear [in their evidence]—﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾ manifest, as a state [of the verses], ﴿those who do not expect the meeting with Us say﴾ ﴿those who do not fear the Resurrection﴾ ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ one in which there is no defamation of ﴿our gods﴾ ﴿or change it﴾ of your own accord. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿It is not for me to change it of my own accord; I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord,﴾ by changing it, ﴿the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 16:

﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it."﴾ (Aʿlamakum, "made you know") ﴿bihi﴾ ("of it"). Wa-lā (nor) is a negative particle conjoined to what precedes it. In another reading, it is with the lām of the response to law (lō), meaning: "Indeed I would have made you know of it through the tongue of another." ﴿Then I have dwelt among you a lifetime﴾ (makath, "I remained") ﴿among you for a lifetime﴾ (sinīna, "years") forty ﴿before it﴾ (lā uḥaddithukum bi-shayʾ, "I did not speak to you of anything"). ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ (annahu laysa min qablī, "that it is not from me before this").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 17:

﴿Who is more unjust﴾, i.e., no one is [more unjust] than ﴿he who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by ascribing a partner to Him, ﴿or denies His signs﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ (i.e., the matter) ﴿does not succeed﴾, i.e., does not attain happiness, ﴿the criminals﴾, i.e., the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 18:

﴿And they worship, besides Allah,﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿that which can neither harm them﴾ if they do not worship Him, ﴿nor benefit them﴾ if they worship it, namely the idols. ﴿And they say﴾ about them, ﴿"These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Do you inform Allah of that which He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ It is an interrogative of denial, for if He had a partner He would know it, since nothing is hidden from Him. ﴿Exalted is He﴾ above it, in glorification of Him, ﴿and high above what they associate with Him.﴾ The particle "mā" here is a relative, and the pronoun ـهُ (in "yushrikūna") refers to what is associated with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 19:

﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ upon one religion, which is Islam, from Adam until Noah. It was said: from the time of Ibrahim (Abraham) until ʿAmr ibn Luhayy. ﴿Then they differed﴾ by some remaining steadfast and some disbelieving. ﴿And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾ concerning the postponement of the recompense until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, i.e., between the people, in this world, ﴿concerning that about which they differ﴾ of the religion, by punishing the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 20:

﴿And they say﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿"Why has not been sent down to him"﴾ i.e., to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"a sign from his Lord?"﴾ just as there were for the prophets, such as the she-camel, the staff and the hand. ﴿So say﴾ to them, ﴿"The unseen belongs only to Allah"﴾ that which is hidden from the servants, i.e., His command, and among it are the signs. So none brings them but Him, and upon me is only the conveying (of the message). ﴿So wait﴾ for the punishment, if you do not believe.

The commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn):

﴿And when We let the people﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿taste mercy﴾, meaning rain and abundance, ﴿after adversity﴾, meaning hardship and drought, ﴿that had touched them﴾, ﴿then they have a scheme against Our signs﴾, by mocking and denying them. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿God is swifter in scheming﴾, as a recompense. ﴿Indeed Our messengers﴾, the guardian angels, ﴿record what you scheme﴾, with the ta' and the ya' (i.e., يَكْتُبُونَ is read with both تَكْتُبُونَ and يَكْتُبُونَ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 22:

﴿He is the One who enables you to travel﴾ on land and sea. In another reading, it is yanshurukum (﴿He spreads you out﴾). ﴿Until, when you are in the ships﴾ (al-fulk: the ships) ﴿and they sail with them﴾ — here there is iltifat (a shift) away from address (from the second person "you" to the third person "them"). ﴿with a good wind﴾, gentle, ﴿and they rejoice in it, there comes upon it a violent wind﴾, strong in its blowing, breaking everything, ﴿and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they have been encompassed﴾ — that is, they have been destroyed — ﴿they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ (ad-du'a': supplication) ﴿saying: "If You deliver us from this﴾ (al-ahwal: these terrors), ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾, the monotheists.

Commentary of al-Maḥallī and al-Suyūṭī (*Tafsīr al-Jalālayn*) on Surah 10, verse 23:

﴿So when He had delivered them, behold, they committed excess in the earth without right﴾, by [associating partners with God] (بِالشِّرْكِ, *bi-l-shirk*). ﴿O mankind, your excess is only against yourselves﴾, meaning your injustice (ظُلْمكُمْ, *ẓulmukum*) is against yourselves, because its sin falls upon them. ﴿It is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾, in which you are given enjoyment for a little. ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾ after death, ﴿and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾, meaning We will recompense you for it.

And in another reading (qirāʾa, a variant recitation of the Qur'an), *matāʿ* (مَتاع) is in the accusative case (*naṣb*), so that the sense is: أَيْ تَتَمَتَّعُونَ (*ay tatamattaʿūna*), that is, "you enjoy."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 24:

﴿Indeed, the likeness﴾ (ṣifa, description) ﴿of the life of this world is like water﴾ (maṭar, rain) ﴿which We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mixed with it﴾ (bisababihi, because of it) ﴿grew thick﴾ (wa-ashtabaka baʿḍuhu bi-baʿḍin, and some of it became intertwined with other parts) ﴿of what men eat﴾ (min al-burr wa-l-shaʿīr wa-ghayrihimā, of wheat, barley and other things) ﴿and livestock﴾ (min al-kalaʾ, of pasture grass). ﴿Until, when the earth took on its adornment﴾ (bahjatuhā min al-nabāt, its splendour from the plants) ﴿and became adorned﴾ (bi-l-zahr, with flowers; its origin is تَزَيَّنَتْ, tazayyanat, in which the tāʾ was replaced by zāy and assimilated into the following zāy) ﴿and its people thought they were able over it﴾ (mutamakkinūna min taḥṣīl thimārihā, capable of gathering its fruits). ﴿Our command came upon it﴾ (qaḍāʾunā aw ʿadhābunā, Our decree or Our punishment) ﴿by night or by day, and We made it﴾ (ayy zarʿahā, that is, its crop) ﴿a harvest﴾ (ka-l-maḥṣūd bi-l-manājil, like that which is cut with sickles) ﴿as if it had not flourished﴾ (ka-an mukhaffafa, that is, ka-annahā, lightened form) ﴿yesterday﴾ (takun, it had not been). ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾ (nubayyin, We make clear).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 25:

﴿And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace﴾ i.e., safety, which is Paradise, by calling to faith. ﴿And He guides whom He wills﴾ to His guidance ﴿to a straight path﴾ the religion of Islam.

(For) those who did good (by believing) is the best reward (al-husna), which is Paradise, and an increase (ziyada), which is looking at Him, Exalted is He, as in the hadith of Muslim. Neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces (la yarhaqu wujuhahum qatar): (qatar means) blackness; nor humiliation (dhilla), (which means) gloom.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 27:

﴿And those who earned evil deeds⦆ — "those who" is conjoined (ʿatf) to "for those who did good" (lil-ladhīna aḥsanū), meaning: and for those who ﴿earned evil deeds﴾, i.e., committed shirk (ʿamilū al-shirk), ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾, ﴿and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah﴾ — min here is extra (zāʾida), and ʿāṣim means one who prevents. ﴿As if their faces had been covered﴾ — ughshiyat, meaning they were clothed (ulbisat) ﴿with pieces of the night, dark﴾ — qiṭaʿan, with the ṭāʾ vowelled with a fatḥa as the plural of qiṭʿa, and also with it sukūn, meaning a portion (juzʾan).

(And) mention the Day We will gather them all (i.e., the creation) together. Then We will say to those who associated partners (with Allah): "Stay in your place, you and your partners (i.e., the idols)." (The word) "stay" is in the accusative, governed by a implied verb, "adhimu" (keep to, remain). "You" is an emphatic affirmation of the hidden pronoun in the implied verb, so that "your partners" can be coordinated with it. "We separated them" means We made a distinction between them and the believers, as in the verse: "And stand apart today, O guilty ones." (Qur'an 36:59) "And their partners will say to them: 'You did not used to worship us'": the "ma" is a negating particle, and the object was placed first for the sake of the verse-ending (fasilah).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 10, verse 29:

﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you, that we were indeed﴾ "in" here is *mukhaffafa* (the lightened form, that is, the lightened *inna*), meaning *innā* (that we are).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 30:

﴿Hunālika﴾ i.e., that day. ﴿Tablū﴾ from al-balwā (testing, putting to the test); and in another reading, with two tā's, from al-tilāwa (recitation): ﴿every soul will experience what it has sent forward﴾, i.e., what it has previously done of deeds. ﴿And they will be returned to God, their true Master﴾, the Real, the Enduring. ﴿And what they used to fabricate﴾ against Him of partners ﴿will be lost to them﴾, i.e., will be absent from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 31:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Who provides for you from the heaven﴾ by means of rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ by means of plants? ﴿Or who controls the hearing﴾ — meaning the ears — that is, who created them, ﴿and the sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who arranges the affair﴾ among the creatures? ﴿They will say﴾ "It is ﴿Allah.﴾" ﴿So say﴾ to them: ﴿Will you not then fear [Him]?﴾ — the pronoun [Him] is omitted — ﴿so that you believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 32:

﴿Then that is⁠ Allah, your Lord, the Truth⁠﴾ — the Doer of these things — ﴿the Truth⁠﴾, the Established One. ﴿So what is there after the truth except error?⁠﴾ This is an interrogative of affirmation, meaning: there is nothing beyond it; so whoever misses the truth, which is the worship of Allah, falls into error. ﴿So how⁠﴾ — how — ﴿are you turned away⁠﴾ from faith ﴿when the proof is established?⁠﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 33:

﴿Thus﴾ as He turned these away from faith, ﴿the word of your Lord has come true against those who defiled themselves﴾ i.e., disbelieved, and it is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell"﴾ the verse, or it is ﴿that they do not believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 34:

﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?" Say: "It is Allah who originates creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded?"﴾ "You are turned away" from His worship, "despite the existence of the proof."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 35:

﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?"﴾ by establishing the proofs and creating guidance. ﴿Say: "Allah guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?"﴾ And He is Allah. ﴿Is He more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance (yahiddi, from yahtadi) unless he is guided?⁠﴾ Is He more worthy to be followed? It is an interrogative of affirmation and rebuke, meaning: the first is more worthy. ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?⁠﴾ This corrupt judgment, namely following what does not deserve to be followed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 36:

﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture﴾ in the worship of idols, ﴿nothing but conjecture﴾, in that they imitated their fathers blindly, ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ in matters where what is required is knowledge, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 37:

﴿And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated﴾ i.e., (it could not be) a fabrication ﴿apart from Allah﴾ i.e., other than Him. ﴿But﴾ it was sent down as ﴿a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾ of the Books, ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾ a clarification of what Allah has prescribed of rulings and other things, ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ no doubt, ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾. It is connected either to "confirmation" or to the omitted "was sent down". It is also read with "confirmation" and "detailed explanation" in the nominative, with the implied subject "it is" (huwa).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 38:

﴿Am﴾ (rather) ﴿they say: "He has invented it."﴾ That is, Muhammad has fabricated it. ﴿Say: "Then bring a surah like it"﴾ in eloquence and rhetorical excellence, as an invention of your own, for you are Arabs, eloquent like me. ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God﴾ to help you in that, that is, other than Him. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in claiming that it is a fabrication, [then do so], but you will not be able to do that.

Rather, they denied that which they had not encompassed in knowledge, that is, the Qur'an, and they did not reflect upon it, and its *ta'wil* (the final outcome or realization of what it contains) had not yet come to them. ﴿Thus did those who came before them deny﴾ their messengers. ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾ who denied the messengers. That is, the final outcome of their affair was destruction. Likewise, We will destroy these (deniers).

And among them are those who believe in it, (meaning) the people of Makkah, [those whom] God knows will believe from among them; and among them are those who will never believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters. (This is) a threat to them.

And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work," meaning: for each is the recompense of their own deeds. "You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do." This is mansūkh (abrogated, a ruling replaced by a later one through naskh) by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 42:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ when you recite the Qur'an. ﴿Can you then make the deaf hear﴾ He likened them to the deaf in their failure to benefit from what is recited to them. ﴿Even though they do not understand﴾ with their deafness, ﴿they do not reflect﴾ (yatadabbarun).

﴿And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾ He likened them to the blind in their failure to be guided, rather, they are worse than the blind.

﴿Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 45:

﴿And on the Day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world or in the graves] except an hour of the day﴾, i.e., as if they (kaʾannahum) ﴿had not remained﴾ [in the world or in the graves] ﴿except an hour of the day﴾ because of the terror of what they saw. The clause of comparison is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun [in "He gathers them"]. ﴿They will recognize one another﴾ [i.e.,] some of them will recognize others when they are resurrected. Then the recognition will cease because of the severity of the terrors. The clause is either a conditioned circumstantial clause (ḥāl muqaddara) or it is attached to the adverbial of time [mutaʿallaq al-ẓarf]. ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost﴾, [meaning] the denial of the resurrection (al-baʿth).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 10, verse 46:

﴿Whether﴾ (wa-immā): there is assimilation (idghām) of the nūn of the conditional particle in (in) into the added (mazīdah) mā. ﴿We show you some﴾ of ﴿what We promise them﴾ of punishment during your life, and the answer of the condition is omitted, meaning: then that is so. ﴿Or We take you (in death)﴾ before their punishment, ﴿then to Us is their return. Then Allah is Witness﴾ (shahīd), Observer ﴿over what they do﴾ of their denial and disbelief, and so He will punish them with the most severe punishment.

For every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, judgment is passed between them with justice, and they are not wronged.

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn) For every nation among the nations there is a messenger; when their messenger comes to them and they deny him, judgment is passed between them with justice, that is, with fairness, so they are punished, and the messenger and those who believed him are saved. "And they are not wronged" by being punished without any crime. Likewise do We deal with these (people).
﴿And they say, "When is this promise"﴾ (of punishment) ﴿"if you are truthful"﴾ about it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 49:

﴿Say: I do not control for myself any harm﴾ (i.e., I cannot repel it) ﴿or any benefit﴾ (i.e., I cannot bring it about) ﴿except what Allah wills﴾ (i.e., that He empowers me to do so). ﴿How then could I control for you the descent of punishment?﴾ ﴿For every nation is a term﴾ (i.e., a known period for their destruction). ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it for an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ (i.e., they cannot go before it).

Say: "Tell me: if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would be hastening to?" (Say, "Inform me," i.e., Tell me.) ﴿If His punishment﴾ i.e., Allah's ﴿comes upon you by night﴾ (bayatan), i.e., at night, ﴿or by day﴾ (naharan). ﴿What is it that the criminals would be hastening to?﴾ i.e., what is it of the punishment that ﴿the criminals﴾, the polytheists, ﴿would be hastening to?﴾ Here the apparent noun has been placed in the position of the pronoun. The interrogative clause is the response (jawab) of the conditional clause, as when you say: "If I come to you, what will you give me?" The purpose of it is to terrify them, i.e., how great is what they were hastening (for).

Then, when it befalls you, [will you believe in it?] — that is, when it has come upon you, [you will say:] "We believe in Him" — i.e., in God, or in the punishment at the time of its descent. The hamza here is for denying the delay, so it will not be accepted from you, and it will be said to you: "Now [you believe], when you used to hasten it in mockery?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 52:

﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of eternity."﴾ That is, the punishment in which you will abide forever. ﴿Are you recompensed except﴾ for what? ("ما" here is interrogative, meaning "what") ﴿ ... except﴾ the recompense [of what you used to earn].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 53:

﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?"﴾ They ask you for information, ﴿"Is it true?"﴾ i.e., what You promised us of the punishment and the resurrection. ﴿Say, "Yes (ii)"﴾ meaning, yes, ﴿"by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape"﴾ from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 54:

﴿And if every soul that had wronged⟩ disbelieved ﴿had everything on the earth⟩ entirely of wealth ﴿it would surely offer it as ransom⟩ from the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And they will conceal the regret⟩ over abandoning faith ﴿when they see the punishment⟩; their leaders concealed it from the weak ones who had led them astray, out of fear of reproach. ﴿And judgment will be passed between them⟩, between the creatures, ﴿with justice⟩, with fairness, ﴿and they will not be wronged⟩ in anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 55:

﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Surely the promise of Allah﴾ of the resurrection and the recompense ﴿is true﴾, established, ﴿but most of them﴾, i.e., the people, ﴿do not know﴾ that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 56:

﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned﴾ in the Hereafter, so He will recompense you for your deeds.

O mankind! (i.e., the people of Mecca) there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord, a Book containing what is beneficial and harmful for you, namely the Qur'an; and a healing (a remedy) for what is in the breasts, from corrupt beliefs and doubts; and guidance from misguidance, and a mercy for the believers in it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 10, verse 58:**

﴿Say: "By the grace of Allah"﴾ — meaning Islam — ﴿and by His mercy﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿so let them rejoice in that﴾ — meaning the grace and the mercy — ﴿it is better than what they accumulate﴾ — from the world. It is read with the **bil-ya'** (with the letter ya', "they rejoice") and **wa'l-ta'** (with the letter ta', "you rejoice").

Qur'an 10:59: ﴿Say: "Have you considered"﴾ tell me ﴿what God has sent down﴾ created ﴿for you of provision, and you made some of it unlawful and lawful﴾ like the *bahirah* (a she-camel whose ear was slit to mark it as dedicated, and left free from work or milking) and the *sa'ibah* (a camel released to roam freely) and the carrion. ﴿Say: "Has God permitted you"﴾ to do that, to make lawful and unlawful? ﴿Or﴾ rather, ﴿against God do you invent lies﴾ by attributing that to Him.

﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against Allah﴾ — that is, what will be their assumption about Him ﴿on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ Do they suppose He will not punish them? No! ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ — by granting them respite and by bestowing blessings upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 61:

﴿And you (O Muhammad) are not engaged in any affair﴾, ﴿and you recite not any Qur'an from Him﴾ (i.e., from the affair, or from Allah) ﴿which He revealed to you﴾, ﴿and you do not do any deed﴾ (addressing him and his community) ﴿except that We are witnesses over you﴾ (watchers) ﴿when you engage in it﴾ (i.e., take up the deed). ﴿And not hidden from your Lord is an atom's weight﴾ (measure) ﴿of an ant (dhharra), the smallest ant﴾ ﴿on the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear Book﴾ (manifest), which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 62:

﴿Truly, the allies of Allah—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ [They will have this] in the Hereafter.
﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of God﴾ [by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 64:

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾ It has been explained, in a hadith whose authenticity was affirmed by al-Hakim, as the good dream that a man sees or that is seen for him. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ [it is] Paradise and reward. ﴿There is no alteration in the words of Allah﴾ there is no breaking of His promises. ﴿That﴾ mentioned [above] is

﴿Let not their speech grieve you﴾, [i.e., their saying to you], "You are not a messenger," and other such things. ﴿Indeed﴾ is a resumption (*isti'naf*, a new independent clause). ﴿Might﴾, meaning power, ﴿belongs to God entirely. He is the All-Hearing﴾ of speech, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of deeds, so He will requite them and grant you victory.

Verily, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, as slaves, possession and creation. And those who call upon (i.e., worship) besides Allah, that is, other than Him, idols as partners to Him in reality, exalted is He above that, do not follow (in that) except conjecture, that is, their assumption that they are gods who will intercede for them. And they are not but guessing, that is, lying in that.

He it is Who made the night for you, that you may rest therein, and the day to see by. [Attributing seeing (al-ibsar) to the day is a metaphor (majaz), because people see in it.] Indeed in that are signs (ayat), i.e., proofs of His Oneness, may He be exalted, for a people who listen (yasma'un), listening with reflection (sama' tadabbur) and taking admonition (ittiʿaz).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 68:

﴿They said﴾ i.e., the Jews and the Christians and whoever claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah, ﴿"Allah has taken a son."﴾ Allah, exalted is He, says to them: ﴿Glory be to Him!﴾ (tanzih), exalting Him above having a son. ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ above every creature; one who needs a son is only someone who is in need of him. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in dominion, creation and servitude. ﴿There is not with you any authority﴾ (hujjah, proof) ﴿for this﴾ which you are saying. ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ This is an interrogative of rebuke (istifham tawbikh).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 69:

﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah﴾ by attributing a child to Him ﴿will not succeed﴾ will not attain happiness.
For them is a little enjoyment in this world, which they enjoy for the duration of their lives. Then to Us is their return by death. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment after death.

﴿And recite﴾ to them, O Muhammad, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿the news﴾, meaning the account, ﴿of Nūḥ (Noah)﴾. It may be a substitute (يُبْدَل, yubdal) for it, ﴿when he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing﴾ (my remaining among you, lubthī) ﴿and my reminding﴾ (my admonishing you, waʿẓī) ﴿of the signs of Allah is burdensome to you, then in Allah I place my trust. So resolve upon your affair﴾, meaning determine upon a course of action you will carry out against me, ﴿and [gather] your partners﴾. The wāw (و) here means "with" (بِمَعْنى مَعَ). ﴿Then let not your affair be a concealed matter for you﴾, meaning hidden, but rather make it manifest and openly confront me with it. ﴿Then carry out your decision against me﴾, meaning proceed with whatever you intend, ﴿and give me no respite﴾, meaning do not delay me, for indeed I do not care about you.

﴿Then if you turn away﴾ from my admonition, ﴿then I have not asked you for any wage﴾, meaning any reward for it, ﴿so turn away﴾. ﴿My reward is not﴾ (i.e., ﴿in﴾ "not" [ma]) ﴿but with﴾ (i.e., my reward is only with) ﴿God﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 73:

﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark﴾ (the ship), ﴿and made them﴾ (i.e., those who were with him) ﴿successors﴾ upon ﴿the earth﴾, ﴿and We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ by the flood. ﴿So look how was the end of those who were warned﴾ from their destruction. Thus We shall do to whoever denies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 74:

﴿Then We sent after him﴾ i.e., Noah, ﴿messengers to their peoples﴾ like Abraham, Hud and Salih, ﴿and they came to them with clear proofs﴾ the miracles, ﴿but they would not have believed in what they had denied before﴾ i.e., before the sending of the messengers to them. ﴿Thus do We seal﴾ We set a seal upon, ﴿the hearts of the transgressors﴾ so they do not accept faith, just as We sealed the hearts of those (earlier ones).

Then after them We sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs (malaʾihi), meaning his people, with Our signs, the nine (al-tisʿ), but they waxed proud (fa-istakbarū), meaning they were arrogant (ʿan) towards belief in them.
﴿So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is clear magic."﴾ Clear, manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 77:

﴿Musa said: "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' — and magicians never prosper."﴾ [Musa said, "Do you say this to the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this sorcery?'" Indeed, it is sorcery, and the one who brought it has prospered, and he has nullified the sorcery of the sorcerers.] The interrogative particle (al-istifham) in both places is for denial (al-inkar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 78:

﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away﴾ to turn us back ﴿from what we found our fathers upon, and that you two may have the greatness﴾ the kingship ﴿in the land﴾ the land of Egypt ﴿but we will not believe you﴾ we will not be ones who affirm you."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 79:

﴿And Pharaoh said, "Bring me every skilled sorcerer."﴾ Outstanding in the knowledge of magic.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 10, verse 80:

﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them﴾ after they had said to him ﴿Either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw﴾:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 81:

﴿Then when they had cast⁠﴾ their ropes and their staffs, ﴿Moses said: "What you have brought is⁠﴾ magic (sihr). ﴾ The interrogative "mā" is a subject (mubtada'), its predicate (khabar) being ﴿what you have brought⁠﴾, and "as-siḥr" is an apposition (badal). In another reading, with a single hamza, it is a declarative statement, and "mā" is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul) serving as subject. ﴿Indeed, Allah will nullify it⁠﴾, i.e., He will annihilate it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 82:

﴿And Allah establishes the truth﴾ — He confirms and makes manifest — ﴿the truth by His words﴾ — by His promises.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 83:

﴿But none believed in Moses except a small group [ṭāʾifa] of the offspring [dhurriyya] of his people﴾, i.e., of Pharaoh's people, ﴿being afraid of Pharaoh and his chiefs that he would afflict them﴾, i.e., turn them away from their religion by torturing them. ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was exalted﴾, arrogant, ﴿in the land﴾, the land of Egypt, ﴿and indeed he was of the transgressors﴾, those who exceed the limit by claiming lordship.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 85:

﴿Then they said, "In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.﴾ That is: do not let them prevail over us, lest they think that they are upon the truth and thus be tempted by us.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary on Surah Yunus (10), verse 87:

﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother: "Take [as] homes for your people in Egypt houses,﴾ "take" (ittakhidha) [homes], ﴿and make your houses a qiblah﴾ a place of prayer in which you pray, ﴿so that you may be secure from fear.﴾ Pharaoh had prevented them from praying. ﴿And establish prayer﴾ complete it, ﴿and give good tidings to the believers﴾ of victory and Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 88:

﴿And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, [You have given them that] so that they may lead astray from Your way."﴾ [That is, from] Your religion. ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾ — i.e., destroy it — ﴿and harden their hearts﴾ — i.e., seal them and make them firm — ﴿so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ — the painful, the one that causes pain. He invoked [this] curse upon them, and Harun said "Amin" to his supplication.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 89:

﴿He said﴾: The Exalted said, ﴿Your supplication has been answered﴾, so their wealth was turned to stone, and Pharaoh did not believe until drowning overtook him. ﴿So go straight﴾ upon the message and the call until the punishment comes to them. ﴿And do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾ in hastening My decree. It is related that [Moses] remained after this for forty years.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 90:

﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his hosts followed them in tyranny and enmity﴾ — lahiqahum (overtook them) — ﴿Pharaoh and his hosts followed them out of rebellion and hostility﴾ — maf'ul lahu (an object of purpose, i.e. a accusative of cause) — ﴿until, when drowning overtook him, he said: "I believe that⁠" — ay bi-annahu (i.e. "that") — and in another reading with a kasra, as a new sentence (isti'nafan) — ﴿there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims﴾. He repeated it so that it would be accepted from him, but it was not accepted. Jibril pushed mud of the sea into his mouth, out of fear that mercy might reach him, and said to him:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 92:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 93:

They did not differ﴾ by some of them believing and some disbelieving, ﴿until knowledge had come to them. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 94:

﴿So if you are⁠ in doubt⁠ (O Muhammad) about what We have sent down to you⁠ of the narratives, hypothetically⁠ ﴾, ﴿then ask those who read the Book﴾, the Torah, ﴿before you﴾. Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 96:

﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justly due﴾ (وجَبَتْ, meaning: became obligatory) ﴿upon them﴾ with the punishment.
﴿And even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾, then faith will not benefit them at that time.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 10, verse 98:

﴿Why did not﴾ (fa-lawlā), meaning: why was it not the case that ﴿a town﴾ (qaryah), its people being intended, ﴿believed﴾ (āmanat) before the torment came upon them, ﴿so that its faith benefited it﴾, ﴿except﴾ (illā), meaning: but, ﴿the people of Yunus (Jonah), when they believed﴾ at the sight of the signs of the torment, and they were not delayed until it arrived, ﴿We removed from them the torment of disgrace in the life of this world and We let them enjoy for a time﴾, meaning: until the completion of their appointed terms.
﴿Had your Lord willed, all who are on earth would have believed, all of them together. Would you then compel people﴾ with what Allah has not willed of them ﴿until they become believers﴾? No.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 100:

﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ by His will, ﴿and He places the defilement﴾ the punishment ﴿upon those who do not use reason﴾ they do not reflect upon the signs of Allah.

Say ﴿Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., of the signs (*ayat*) that point to the oneness (*wahdaniyya*, tawhid, the affirmation of God's unity) of Allah the Exalted, addressing the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And signs and warnings avail not﴾, the word *nudhur* being the plural of *nadhir* (warner), i.e., the messengers, ﴿for a people who will not believe﴾ in the knowledge of Allah, i.e., they do not benefit them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 10, verse 102:

﴿Then do they await﴾ (فَهَلْ) — i.e., (فَما) what — ﴿but the like of the days of those who passed away before them﴾ (يَنْتَظِرُونَ) (by rejecting you)? — from the nations; i.e., the like of their incidents of punishment. ﴿Say: "Then wait﴾ for that; (فانْتَظِرُوا) ...

﴿Then We save﴾ The present tense (*al-muḍāriʿ*, the imperfect verb form) is used to narrate a past event (*ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍī*), ﴿Our messengers and those who believe﴾ from the punishment. ﴿Thus﴾ the saving, ﴿it is incumbent upon Us; We save the believers﴾: the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, at the time when the polytheists were being punished.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 104:

﴿Say: "O mankind"﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿"if you are in doubt about my religion"﴾, [doubting] that it is true, ﴿"then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah"﴾, i.e., other than Him, which are the idols, because of your doubt concerning it. ﴿"But I worship Allah, who causes you to die"﴾, who seizes your souls. ﴿"And I have been commanded that"﴾, i.e., "to"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 105:

And (it was said to me): "That I should set my face toward the religion, inclining to it as a true monotheist (ḥanīfan)," meaning: inclining toward it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 106:

﴿Do not call upon﴾ (i.e., worship) ﴿besides Allah that which neither benefits you﴾ if you worship it ﴿nor harms you﴾ if you do not worship it. ﴿But if you did﴾ that, hypothetically.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 107:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾ He afflicts you ﴿with harm﴾ such as poverty or sickness, ﴿there is no remover﴾ lifter ﴿of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, there is no repeller﴾ averter ﴿of His bounty﴾ which He intends for you ﴿that He causes it to reach﴾ i.e., the good.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 108:

﴿Say, "O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided, he is guided only for [the benefit of] himself, and whoever goes astray only errs to its detriment. And I am not over you a guardian."﴾ [i.e., over the people of Makkah]. ﴿Whoever is guided, he is guided only for himself﴾ because the reward of his guidance is for him. ﴿And whoever goes astray, he only goes astray to its detriment﴾ because the harm of his misguidance falls upon him. ﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾ so that I would compel you to guidance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 10, verse 109:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you﴾ from your Lord, ﴿and be patient﴾ over the call and their harm, ﴿until Allah judges﴾ between them by His command, ﴿and He is the best of judges﴾, the most just of them. And he was patient until judgment was passed upon the polytheists to be fought, and upon the People of the Book to pay the jizya (poll tax).
